title: The journey of one token
description: Step through the boundaries between message, state, execution and output.
assumptions: The path is a teaching sketch; a real engine has loops, branches and several modes.
task: Write down the input and output of every step, then propose one failure case for one of the arrows.

title: From logits to probabilities
description: Tune the temperature and the random number; see how the distribution differs from the draw.
assumptions: Uses only three scores; does not simulate the full top-k / top-p / penalty chain.
task: Fix u and change the temperature, then fix the temperature and change u. Explain which one changes the distribution.

title: Work out a matrix multiplication
description: Change the input and see each row's dot product and the output shape.
assumptions: A teaching GEMV on a fixed 2×3 matrix; it does not measure hardware speed.
task: Predict the result on paper first, then change one input element and see which outputs change.

title: Bits and quantization error
description: Watch outliers, bit width, scale and MSE interact.
assumptions: Symmetric uniform quantization; not the IQ family or a real KV format.
task: Record the error at 2, 4 and 8 bits, then add an outlier and compare the cost of a shared scale.

title: Compute or bandwidth?
description: Compute the theoretical lower bound and the Amdahl overall speedup together.
assumptions: Bandwidth and compute are input assumptions; the fixed overhead cannot be hidden; this does not predict a real GPU.
task: Double the speed of one stage and see why the end-to-end gain does not double.

title: One recurrent update
description: A one-dimensional GDN; compare the correct and the wrong update order.
assumptions: One scalar state only; no real multiple heads, projections, convolution or normalization.
task: Set α=0, β=0 or k=0 and check each boundary property one by one.

title: Cache traces and conflicts
description: Compare LRU, LFU, FIFO and 8-way rotation on the same trace.
assumptions: Not the upstream adaptive expert policy; sets are picked by integer modulo, not the upstream mix.
task: With 16 slots and 9 odd keys in the same set, compare fully associative LRU with 8-way rotation.

title: Splitting work between CPU and GPU
description: Change the split ratio and find the ideal balance between the two branches.
assumptions: The two branches are assumed independent and their effective rates are inputs; real DRAM contention is ignored.
task: Halve the effective rate of the PCIe branch and explain why an even split no longer works.

title: Chunking and the space trade-off
description: Pick a feasible chunk under an explicit teaching cost curve.
assumptions: The reuse curve and per-token scratch are made-up parameters; this is not an allocator simulation.
task: Find the fastest chunk first, then rule out the ones over budget, and compare the best feasible with the absolute best.

title: History state budget
description: Use the fixed geometry to compute the main KV, the resident window and the main GDN state.
assumptions: The quantization metadata ratio is a made-up estimate; full engine overhead is not counted, and the lab does not imply every format combination is supported.
task: Change 32K to 128K, then make it five active sequences, and check the bytes and GiB.

title: How long a draft is worth guessing
description: Compare the expected tokens, time and net gain for k=0…5.
assumptions: One conditional acceptance rate p for every position; the cost is a linear teaching formula, not the full upstream CostModel.
task: Set p=0 and p=1, then raise the draft cost, and confirm the controller can fall back to no draft.

title: Commit only the accepted prefix
description: Shows why the candidate state and the committed state differ.
assumptions: Toy recurrence s←0.5s+t; does not simulate Verifier row 0 or the target token offset.
task: Make the second draft get rejected, and point out which wrong state is left behind if you roll back only the counter.

title: Byte chunks are not events
description: Cut a Chinese text stream into pieces of any length and rebuild the events incrementally.
assumptions: A data-only JSON SSE subset that handles LF/CRLF for this example; no full EventSource reconnection.
task: Try every chunk size from 1 byte to 32 bytes; the output must stay the same two Chinese characters.

title: Why short requests keep waiting
description: Compare FCFS and round-robin on first-token time, completion time and switching cost.
assumptions: All requests are ready at t=0, 1 token = 1 ms, no real GPU batching or prefill.
task: Raise the switching cost and watch the trade-off between better fairness and total throughput.
